provenanceClassifiedEvidence.claim: SafeExecutor.validateCommand()/isCommandAllowed() authorize a command string based on path.basename() equality against the allowlist, with no requirement that a path-like command string match an allowlist entry exactly.

OpenClaw (a comparable agentic tool) shipped and fixed a CVSS 9.8 exec-allowlist-bypass vulnerability in the same class (allowlist pattern-matching overmatches the intended scope) in 2026, CVE-2026-32973 / GHSA-f8r2-vg7x-gh8m; Cursor shipped a related terminal-allowlist bypass fix, CVE-2026-22708 / GHSA-82wg-qcm4-fp2w.
provenanceClassifiedEvidence.source: WebSearch + WebFetch tonight: https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/openclaw-exec-allowlist-pattern-overmatch-via-posix-path-normalization , https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/advisories/GHSA-f8r2-vg7x-gh8m , https://github.com/cursor/cursor/security/advisories/GHSA-82wg-qcm4-fp2w — grade A (official GitHub Security Advisories, cross-checked against VulnCheck/NVD listings for CVE-2026-32973)

provenanceClassifiedEvidence.claim: Baseline (git HEAD) decision-boundary ASR against a 5-case basename-collision corpus = 100% (5/5 authorized). Candidate ASR = 0% (0/5). Legitimate bare-name usage pass rate unchanged at 100% (4/4) on both. Real end-to-end proof-of-exploit: baseline actually executes a planted sentinel binary at a spoofed path; candidate throws COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED before spawning it.

12/12 manually-reconstructed assertions from the repo's own __tests__/safe-executor.test.ts pass against the candidate (empty-allowlist, dangerous-command-in-allowlist, argument injection patterns, sudo blocking, factory functions all unaffected).

Bounded 1-generation/3-variant exploration confirms the shipped fix (Variant A) is the fitness-maximizing formulation among 3 real, independently-executed alternatives (fitness 1.00 vs 0.98 vs 0.795).

Any future caller in this repo or a downstream plugin that derives a `command` string dynamically (from a resolved PATH lookup, a config file, or any value not a compile-time string literal) and passes it to a bare-name-allowlisted SafeExecutor would, pre-fix, be exploitable by anything able to influence that derivation to point at an attacker-controlled path.
provenanceClassifiedEvidence.basis: no current in-repo caller does this (confirmed by grep across v3/ for SafeExecutor construction/usage), so this is a defense-in-depth closure of a latent bypass surface in a documented, reusable security primitive — not a fix for an actively-exploited path in this checkout tonight.

provenanceClassifiedEvidence.claim: Requiring exact-match for any path-like `command` string (while preserving basename leniency for bare names) eliminates the basename-collision bypass class with zero regression to today's real callers.
Ship Variant A, scoped to v3/@claude-flow/security/src/safe-executor.ts only (validateCommand + isCommandAllowed).
provenanceClassifiedEvidence.rationale: highest Darwin-scored fitness among real, executed alternatives; smallest diff that fully closes the demonstrated bypass with no compatibility loss versus real (grep-confirmed) callers

provenanceClassifiedEvidence.claim: Variant B (always-exact-match, drop basename leniency even for bare names)
provenanceClassifiedEvidence.rationale: ties Variant A on safety (5/5 attack cases blocked) but offers zero marginal security benefit while removing a documented convenience with no in-repo caller depending on it either way — strictly dominated by A on fitness (0.98 vs 1.00).

provenanceClassifiedEvidence.claim: Variant D (reject all path-like commands outright, even exact allowlist matches)
provenanceClassifiedEvidence.rationale: ties Variant A on safety but breaks the legitimate exact-path-allowlist-entry pattern (`allowedCommands: ['/usr/bin/git']` + command `/usr/bin/git`) that both baseline and Variant A correctly allow — real quality loss for no safety gain (fitness 0.795).

securityReview.notes: This candidate IS the security-sensitive surface — SafeExecutor is @claude-flow/security's documented command-injection remediation primitive (CLAUDE.md: 'SafeExecutor — Command injection protection'), used in v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/proxy/{install,release}.ts for real subprocess execution (tar/powershell/gh extraction of downloaded release archives). The fix narrows an authorization check (fail-closed direction: previously-allowed inputs become rejected, never the reverse) — the safer direction for a security control to move in. No new filesystem, network, or credential surface is touched; no MCP tool authority is granted or changed. The .harness/mcp-policy.json posture (defaultDeny, allowShell:false at the MCP layer) is unaffected since this fix lives entirely in the native-Claude-Code-reachable @claude-flow/security package, outside MCP-tool jurisdiction.
